messages.subject: Subread subjunc and featureCounts for small RNA sequencing data
messages.subject_clean: Subread subjunc and featureCounts for small RNA sequencing data
messages.body_plain:
I am attempting to use Subread subjunc and featureCounts with small RNA sequencing data and will appreciate comments on appropriate usage of the programs.

--

My data is single-end 50 b-long reads obtained on the Illumina HiSeq 2500 platform with small RNA sequencing libraries (Illumina TruSeq Small RNA Sample Prep kit). It is trimmed to remove adapter and poor-quality sequences (the size of reads thus ranges from 15-50 b).

My main goal is to quantify microRNA (miR) expression. Mature miRs are ~18-22 b in length. They are generated from ~70-90 b-long precursor miRs (pre-miRs) which in turn are produced from primary miR transcripts (pri-miRs) which are like coding RNA transcripts in terms of length. Mature miRs can differ from each other at just one nucleotide position. Different mature miRs (i.e., arising from different pri-miRs) can have the exact same sequence and a pri-miR can produce multiple different mature miRs. Finally, a pri-miR can be the product of multiple copies of a gene.

The reads in my data represent not only mature miRs but also other small RNAs like tRNAs and snoRNAs as well as degradation fragments of coding RNAs (mRNAs), ribosomal RNAs, pre-miRs, pri-miRs, etc., because the biomaterial that were used were formalin-fixed tissues (formalin causes RNA degradation).

So, besides quantifying mature miR expression, I also want to check how many of the reads map to tRNAs, snoRNAs, rRNAs, mRNAs, etc.

--

Considering the above aspects, I am using Subread subjunc to map the reads against the hg19 human genome with:

subjunc -T 16 -i hg19 -r sample.fastq -d 15 -D 50 -B 16 -o sample.bam --BAMoutput

I find that ~70% of the 7-17 million reads of my samples get mapped. I then use featureCounts to obtain counts for miRs using a GFF file from the miR sequence repository (miRBase):

featureCounts -T 16 -a hsa_mir.gff3 -t miRNA -f -O -M -d 15 -D 50 -o sample_mir_count.txt sample.bam

--

I will appreciate if someone can comment on the use of subjunc and featureCounts for small RNA mapping and counting in the manner noted above fashion.

Thanks.

messages.subject: Re: Subread subjunc and featureCounts for small RNA sequencing data
messages.subject_clean: Subread subjunc and featureCounts for small RNA sequencing data
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

You should not use '-d' and '-D' parameters in your subjunc command, since these parameters are for paired end reads. Also, subjunc does not support '-B' option, which is an option supported by subread-align for reporting multiple best mapping locations. But anyway, removing these three parameters from your command wouldn't change your mapping results.

You may also try to run subread-align on your data. Subread-align is more sensitive than subjunc but it still has good specificity. You should get more mapped reads from using subread-align.

Similarly, please do not include '-d' and '-D' options in your featureCounts command.

Hope this helps.

Wei

messages.subject: New release - Subread 1.4.4
messages.body_plain:
Dear All,

We have just released version 1.4.4. Changes and new features can be found below:

(1) Improved featureCounts in processing GTF/GFF format annotation files.
(2) Breakpoint locations are reported along with mapping location of each fusion read in SAM/BAM files, using tags including CC(chromosome name), CP(mapping position), CG(CIGAR string) and CT(strand).
(3) Strandness of the exon-splicing site is reported using XA tag (e.g. XA:A:+) in Subjunc program.
(4) Fragments (ie. read pairs), instead of reads, are counted for each chromosomal location for SNP calling in exactSNP, when paired-end read data are provided.
(5) Full index can be built for a reference genome by subread-buildindex program (no gap between neighbouring subreads) to further reduce the read mapping time.
(6) New utility programs were added, including 'coverageCount' (calcuate coverage at each chromosomal location in a highly efficient manner) and 'propmapped' (cacluate proportion of mapped reads in a SAM/BAM file).
(7) Bug fixes.

Please let us know if you found any bugs or have any suggestions.

Best wishes,

The Subread Team

messages.subject: Re: featureCounts freeing memory twice
messages.body_plain:
Hi Rory,

Firstly, we found that samtools sort -n could incorrectly pair up reads when reads were reported multiple times in a SAM/BAM file (multi-mapping). For example, a read pair could be incorrectly sorted like below by samtools sort -n (note that R1_1 and R1_2 are from the same pair and they have the same read name)

R1_1
R1_1
R1_2
R1_2

featureCounts uses extra information in SAM/BAM files to correctly sort these reads, including read mapping locations, NH tag and HI tag.

When there are reads which were found to have missing mates, featureCounts will also start sorting process to try to find their mates. If their mates are indeed missing, featureCounts will add 'dummy mates' for them, save them to an intermediate file (the sorting result is always saved to an intermediate file by featureCounts) and then count reads from using this intermediate file.

The sorting procedure carried out by featureCounts is to ensure paired end reads are properly sorted and read counting is correctly performed.

Best regards,

Wei

messages.subject: About the -u and -H options for Subread aligner
messages.subject_clean: About the -u and -H options for Subread aligner
messages.body_plain:
The Subread user guide mentions recommends enabling '-u option (reporting uniquely mapped reads only) and also -H option (breaking ties using Hamming distance), when running Subread and Subjunc aligners.'

Does it mean that some reads get mapped as 'uniquely mapped' because of a better Hamming distance when they actually do not map uniquely? And when Hamming distances are equal -- i.e., a tie cannot be broken -- is a read not mapped when -u is on?

I am using Subread with -u and -H on for analyzing sequence polymorphisms. I am concerned about reads from multi-copy genes such as those for ribosomal RNAs and protein. A read indicating a possible SNP could truly map to the correct region it is from, or it could get mapped to a region for a very similar copy of the gene where the SNP-related nucleotide change is normal.

Perhaps what I want to know is if Subread can be made to align reads with (1) zero tolerance for any mismatch (filtering out reads whose mapping requires a mismatch), (2) while requiring absolutely unique mapping.

Thanks.

messages.subject: Re: About the -u and -H options for Subread aligner
messages.subject_clean: About the -u and -H options for Subread aligner
messages.body_plain:
Subread/subjunc aligners use extracted subreads (16 mers) to vote for the mapping location of a read and no mismatches are allowed when mapping these subreads to the reference genome. The location which receives the largest number of votes will be selected as the mapping location for the read. If there are more than one such location found, we call this read a multi-mapping read.

If -H is specified along with -u, subread/subjunc will try to break the tie by choosing the location which have the smallest Hamming distance. If there is still more than one such location, subread/subjunc will report the read as an unmapped read.

We are now working on adding a new parameter to subread/subjunc to allow users to specify the minimum number of mismatches allowed in the reported alignments.

Hope this clarify things.

Wei
